questions.title: Hormone acting by the IP3-Ca2+ mechanism
questions.question: Which of the following hormones acts by the IP3-Ca2+ mechanism?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cholecalciferol (vitamin D) is lipophilic and acts through an intracellular nuclear receptor (the vitamin D receptor) to regulate gene transcription, not through IP3-calcium at the membrane.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Progesterone is a steroid; it crosses the membrane and binds an intracellular nuclear receptor that regulates transcription, so it uses no membrane second messenger.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Insulin binds a receptor tyrosine kinase that autophosphorylates and recruits IRS proteins; its signalling is through the tyrosine-kinase cascade, not IP3-calcium.
explanations.D: Correct. GnRH is a hydrophilic decapeptide that binds a Gq-coupled receptor on the pituitary gonadotroph. Gq activates phospholipase C, which splits PIP2 into inositol trisphosphate (IP3) and diacylglycerol; IP3 releases calcium from intracellular stores and DAG activates protein kinase C, together driving LH and FSH release. This IP3-calcium pathway is the defining second-messenger mechanism of GnRH and separates it from the nuclear-receptor steroids and the tyrosine-kinase insulin among the options.

questions.learning_objective: Identify GnRH as a hormone signalling through the Gq / phospholipase C / IP3-calcium pathway rather than cyclic AMP, a nuclear receptor or a tyrosine kinase.

questions.title: Hormone with intrinsic lactogenic activity
questions.question: Which of the following hormones has intrinsic lactogenic activity?

explanations.A: Incorrect. TSH stimulates the thyroid follicular cells to make thyroid hormone; it has no action on the breast and no lactogenic activity.
explanations.B: Incorrect. MSH acts on melanocytes to promote pigmentation; it is not lactogenic.
explanations.C: Correct. Growth hormone belongs to one structurally homologous family with prolactin and human placental lactogen, so it can bind the prolactin receptor and possesses intrinsic lactogenic activity in addition to its somatotropic effects. This family homology is why marked growth-hormone excess can be associated with galactorrhoea even without a rise in prolactin, and it is what makes GH the lactogenic hormone among these options.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Dopamine is the tonic hypothalamic inhibitor of prolactin release, the opposite of a lactogenic agent.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise growth hormone as the anterior-pituitary hormone with intrinsic lactogenic activity, reflecting its structural homology with prolactin.

questions.title: Plasma carrier of ADH
questions.question: ADH circulates in plasma primarily:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Neurophysin I is the carrier peptide paired with oxytocin, not with ADH.
explanations.B: Correct. Antidiuretic hormone (vasopressin) is synthesised in hypothalamic magnocellular neurons as part of a larger precursor that also yields its specific carrier peptide, neurophysin II. The hormone is transported down the hypothalamo-hypophyseal tract, stored in the posterior pituitary and released bound to neurophysin II, which is its principal association in the circulation. The specific ADH-neurophysin II pairing (versus oxytocin-neurophysin I) is the point tested here.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Plasma albumin and specific globulins carry lipophilic steroid and thyroid hormones; ADH is associated with its own peptide carrier, neurophysin II.
explanations.D: Incorrect. ADH is not simply free in plasma; it is released and associated with neurophysin II derived from its common precursor.

questions.learning_objective: State that ADH (vasopressin) is carried on neurophysin II, derived from its own precursor, in contrast to oxytocin on neurophysin I.
